data: This is a fantastic game, well worth the full price of admission,
I love this game, it's fun it's challenging and there is a ton of content
Amazing gameplay, amazing graphics, amazing soundtrack and amazing selection of different races
One of the best games out there, the lore is absolutely fantastic and stunning
outstanding, better with mods, 10/10, an all time classic
I do not recommend buying this game for more than 20 euros with all DLCs - it's just not worth it
The DLC content is not worth the price and there is way too much

Can we have a "Meh" button?

This is meh. There's some initial fun here, but the replayability is severely limited due to the sub-standard battle mechanics, the frustratingly stupid seige mechanics, and the limited number of unit types to choose from without mods.

Probably the worst of the total war games IMO. (Haven't played Brittania, but I hear it's not amazing either.)

Going to go back to Rome 2. At least in that game a seige felt like a seige instead of a wall rush with badly designed choke points and lack of functional defensive units.

Gonna give it a recommend anyway since I love the TW series, and because the campaign was largely fun (if not lore consistent... I played by autoresolving battles once I had full stacks of elites and a decent economy).

Replayability IMO is very limited.

2000+ hours and over 300 mods tested and i would recommend this game to anyone wanting to command large armies and watch their empire grow over the span of days and weeks of real time. not for those looking for a quick 1v1 campaign or massive online experience. But the visuals are stunning and the game has next to no game braking bugs other then mod compatibility.

I play this game, from time to time... just casually :D Love it 100x more thanks to Venris and his SFO mod, as I am playing 95% of the time as the Vampire Counts or Von Carstein, which could get some loving, from CA.

Hope WH 3 will be a blast ;)

11 out of 10 from me :)

Great game and the only reason im leaving a bad review is that using both Denuvo DRM so you cant play offline and relying on external servers (Epic Games) for game data is a horrible single player experience when you either have internet problems or their own servers stop working.
Lets not mention that they will only address this "after the holidays" when this isnt balancing or some random game bug, its an infrastructure problem that stops you from accessing both your saves and DLC.

As a long time historical fan of the Total War series (started playing Rome 1 around 2006), I was highly skeptical of the extension Creative Assembly was making into the Warhammer univerise, as I knew nothing about it at the time. I'm very happy to be wrong about my initial skepticism. Warhammer II is, in my opinion, the best Total War game to date. The variety, differences and the world itself are so unique that each playthrough is different and interesting.

I highly reccommend this game to anyone who's on the fence about this game.

Easily the best Total War game up to now: The Campaign Mechanics sync beautifully with the Battle Mechanics. There are a LOT of DLCs, but don't be dissuaded: this isn't Paradox, so few, if any, are required to get a really good experience here. This is mainly since all of the DLCs also came with Free Updates that made the base game better without punishing you for not shelling out more money!

The best way to experience it, however, is to also own Total War: Warhammer 1, as this grants you access to a unique Game Mode that combines the campaigns of both games!

Super fun; my first total war titles, but really grabbed my attention early. At first I skipped every fight/auto-completed each fight cos I had no clue what was going on, but over time I have developed a taste for the details of land fights and can't see myself stopping any time soon.

I will not act like this game isn't expensive when it all adds up, but it is really good and really detailed.

I would recommend playing and getting the DLC of the first Warhammer game, before getting this as the DLC is transferable between games. (Yes. including the third one.)

Good game, bad sales practice. I enjoyed the main campaign, and wanted to play Mortal Empires. I load up the game after installing the "free" content. But then, I am immediately hit with a pop up that says WARNING ownership of Total War Warhammer 1 is required to play the Mortal Empires campaign. I was fortunate in that I discovered this during a Total War franchise sale, so the whole ordeal only set me back 14.99. I am putting this out there so that I can hopefully keep some of my fellow players from falling into the same trap. If you are okay with forgoing the expansion or shelling out more money, I WOULD recommend.

Must have for any fan of the Warhammer franchise and a easy grab for any total war or RTS fan. The differing races allow for a multitude of different playstyles both on and off the battlefield and there is such a wide range of technologies, it creates so many different possibilities
As of this review I'd call this the best Total War game. It is the result of decades of iterative design improvements of the total war style mechanics plus the rich variety of the warhammer universe.

its fun and all, but HOLY CHRIST ARE THE LOADING SCREENS LONG, i'm literally waiting for 10 fucking minutes in loading screens oh my god. Better have a godly pc and installed on an ssd because this loading screen shit will add up to HOURS quickly.

Imagine a good ol' vanilla milkshake blended perfectly with Oreo sandwich cookies.
Total War: WARHAMMER perfectly embodies that as the match made in nirvana.

Strategy lovers need to play this game and have a a try at least once in their life!

One of the coolest and most unique games I've played. The battles play out like movies and the variety is fantastic. I LOVE using the AI General mod with many others to play like a third person RPG.

...Yes, you can play this game in third person mode and yes, you can pretty much control any character.

Don't use Kaedrin Mod Manager or you'll likely break your game.
its a very great game, even without the dlc its a great game, full of stories, battles and adventures
This is hard af but so much fun!!!! ive been playing on easy X2 and its still hard!!
If you like RTS games this game will give you hundreds of hours of fun. if you dont like RTS games, theres a chance this game could sway your opinion.

I'm personally new to the series and haven't played TWW1 or TWW3 but as a standalone game it has a lot of variety with many playable factions even if you don't spend any money on DLC. The big thing for me was having to pretty much study for a few days before even understanding how the game works to a decent level, but after finding my footing it's very fun. Fairly diverse and interesting range of modded content too which I always like to see for little tweaks and such.

Simply one of the best strategy games ever made. There is a staggering amount of content that can keep you entertained for hours. Not to mention the variety between all the different races.

This is the game you should pick up if you've always been interested in strategy games, but never 'bitten the bullet'.

Make sure to pick up Total War: Warhammer I for the Mortal Empires combined map for an incredible experience that is only going to get better with the release of Total War: Warhammer III next month.

10/10 would buy all the DLC again

Really fantastic and my go-to strategy game. Compared to other Total War games I've played, Warhammer's most fun in its core gameplay loop, just normal field battles - the 'rock, paper, scissors' approach is really enlivened with monsters, flying units, and wizards. Warhammer is also great in terms of variety of units and the aesthetics of different factions.

What could be improved, lots of people say sieges, but having played '3 Kingdoms' a bit, I'd really love a few more diplomatic options. I understand some grand factions can be completely incompatible with one another, but I'd love internally within a faction to have some options. (There's been several times playing as the High Elves, Tyrion fights me for control of Ulthuan and we should just be out there fighting our common enemies).

Happily spent a thousand hours across WH1 & 2, looking forward to another thousand with WH3!

Had the game forever, but it still needs Total War Warhammer 1 to have Immortal Empire work, I got the game but it must be installed as well to access this feature. But why though? Warhammer 3 doesn't need 1 and 2, so why does 2 need 1?
Waste of 30gb and a hassle in the library department. Just get Total War Warhammer 3 at this point and purchase past DLC's there.

This game was very disappointing. The warfare is all with medieval technology making it practically the same as historical total war games. It seems that the whole total war series is just cookie cutter games with only superficial differences, like your girlfriend changing her dress and her name and then saying you've got a new girlfriend. I had played total war Rome II prior and the gameplay in this game felt identical. I completely lost interest in the total war series after noticing this.

A great Total War game. Lot's of variety to the units and factions drawn from classic Warhammer fantasy lore.

The only real issue is that after 3+ years it has become a little heavy on the DLC but you don't need to buy them all to experience most of the content.
very limited gameplay without mortal empires. I detest the launcher, and the money grabbing tactics.

At first i said ffffff this is really hard. I left it. Then I returned and made friends, tried not to have many enemies, built walls... Then I bought a dlc that fitted me (the one with the trees). Amazing game, great time, really strategic and not just oooo I have the biggest and strongest army let's conquer everything. Nope you have to play smart and be careful.
If I had to pick one game from my library to play for ever it would be this one. Every time I go to buy a new game I think ‘I havnt played tw wh2 enough’ buy the dlc on sale coz there overpriced af.

Really great game. Especially fun if you can play with buddy's but be warned sometimes the campaign can take a while, which is great because it is a lot of fun but be ready to be in it for the long haul.

There are no good total war games because they are all fundamentally flawed. They get old very quickly when you realize that every 'start' is just a limitation that you need to strategize around instead of being like an actual strategy game such as Eu4 or even RTS games where you can adapt meaningfully. Every turn in every total war game plays the same because you either stick to a strategy or get blown out on a 'hard' start since you didn't watch or read a reddit post telling you exactly what to do.

What can I say, this game has eaten hundreds of my hours and in all honesty, I always want to come back. Try new units, a new legendary lord, a new build idea on an old favorite. It's superb and I don't see myself stopping until 3 comes out.
its a fun game and i like the free legendary lords, i'd recommend this over TW3 as you get more lord options and it runs much better

This game is so good its got me interested in the actual table top game, obviously not 40K but Age Of Sigmar. My favourite faction might be Skaven or Lizardmen they're so awesome. Also when i started playing more than a year a go my HDD could not handle it so I did recently upgrade to a SSD and I think its a must trust me.

My favourite Total War ever. I love it, it's great, it's the most amazing thing ever, it has beautiful people in it, yes I am talking about you, the moders, but also the characters, that make this game, great. Absolutely, great.

Thank you.

My best friend bought this for me years ago, and it was my jumping on point for Warhammer. At first I was playing it strictly because I liked the Total War gameplay, but after enough time I developed an interest in the lore and the universe, and 40K after that. I love the sheer number of options available in a game of Immortal Empires, and it kept me entertained for like a thousand hours. Great game.

Deceptive marketing from this company. This isn't a true part 2, this is essentially a standalone expansion / game update that they put up for sale as a part 2 to trick newcomers to the series. You think you can skip part 1, but this game is missing key features like a conquest mode and half the races unless you purchase the first one and all of its DLCs retroactively.

Of course long time fans who have owned the first game all along don't mind, but this is a really dishonest way to make people think they can get into the series late and then ambush them with an entire extra game worth of DLC that doesn't show up on the store page.

If they had simply released this as an expansion to Total War: Warhammer I wouldn't have an issue with it, you'd know that what you're really dealing with is one huge living game with a massive backlog of DLC and you'd know what to buy if you want to try the basics. But this makes you purchase a specialty campaign with only half the races in it, and doesn't tell you that the meat and potatoes of the game where you fight over the whole world and can play any race you want costs extra.

The game is fun. better with the right mods like army upkeep for one. the siege battles leave a lot to be desired which is odd comming from a Total War game. I like the High Elves the best but have played all of the factions in length. the end times invasion is a lot better then it was in WHTW1 and can wipe you out if you aren't prepared for it. the multiplayer is also fun i find its pretty well balanced. as far as if I think someone should pick it up if you like Total War games you won't like the aforementioned siege battles and CA has really stream lined the campaign management of settlements. that can be see as a good or bad thing. but with all the said yeah i would recommend playing this game and all its DLC i can say a lot more about the game but ill leave it at that.

I still love the warhammer series, yes there are less updates in the 3 at thw moment, but for someone who havebt played before, i think the 2 iand some of its DLC is still a very good starting point, depending on what races interests you! I have played more than 400 hours and i enjoyed all of it, there is a lot of replayability. It is my first big strategy game I have bought and I really don't regret doing the leap. It was hard at first, but once you start understanding the strategies of battle, everything is well. There are often some sales, it's really worth it picking it up on sale. I also recomend the prophet and the warlock DLC for the people that are interested by skaven and lizardmen ;)
You can summon the elector counts, kill the elector counts, eat the elector counts, raise the elector counts as undead or just kill everything without a beard

This game is almost certainly the best addition to the entire Total War series, since Shogun 2. It's also very likely that this game has gotten me into both Warhammer Fantasy & 40k on the whole (albeit, I already knew about some of it via my friends) - so be prepared for that if you're joining purely from a Total War player standpoint.

The 'BLOOD FOR THE BLOOD GOD II' Blood & Gore DLC is an absolute m u s t . It really adds to the effect of someone being eaten by a dragon - (or any other large reptilian for that matter). Also, a big reason it is separate from the actual game itself is that certain countries with certain censorship regulations would ban the game if it were simply included - so the DLC just gets banned instead.

One of the best RTS games I have ever played. If you love Warhammer and RTS, even if it's a 'No-Go' for Warhammer, you should buy Total War: Warhammer II.

With a massive campaign map, fleshed out story, rich diversity of characters and units, active modding community, and inuitive design; I have to commend Creative Assembly / Sega for their handywork. This game is such a masterpiece compared to much of what we see released in the market. They really have taken the better aspects of their previous game and stitched them into a wonderful package. There is also a hefty chunk of Free DLC, which is appreciable. The biggest drawback however is they are primarily TW:Warhammer I attached, meaning you need the original game as well to use them. That and the price.

But honestly, even without the TW:W1 content and the price (get it on sale), it is well worth it. What a great game.

Visuals: 10
Gameplay: 10
Story: 10
Controls: 10
Replayability: 10

ugh, maybe im bias. Just go buy it.

It's a great game that really makes you think about the decisions you make in battle and conquest. Each unit has it's strengths and weaknesses as well as terrain where they can be better or worse. If you like to make better tactical decisions as you play this is a game for you.
Huge armies really tiny on your screen smashing into each other. Whats not to love.

Incredible game with small weaknesses.
Pros:
- huge unit variety
- fun gameplay
- spells and monsters are a blast to play with
- long term support with lots of quality dlc
- really fun way to introduce you to the warhammer universe with lots of interesting characters
- lots of good mods to customize the game to better suit your taste
- great community online
- lizards riding bigger lizards fighting ratmen that use nuclear weapons while there is vampire pirates
somewhere raiding some poor humans and elves fighting emo elves, the game is crazy and lots of fun.
- did I mention you can make comets fall from the sky or summon a giant magical orc that stomps on your
enemies?

Cons:
- bad optimization(rtx3080, 5800x still cant get stable 60+ fps in huge battles on 1440p)
- diplomacy is mediocre
- AI really stupid in certain areas (siege behavior etc.)
- city management is very basic

All in all I don't regret a single hour I put into this game and can't wait for game 3!
great game, especially paired with steel&faith grimhammer mod. lot of factions and replayability potential, though some mechanics/lords are locked behind the dlc's, which can be annoying,
It's good, even great. Sadly CA dropped the ball with the third installment so it will never get the sequel it deserves.
Buy and play Warhammer II for the next 6 months until they improve Warhammer 3.

If you like fantasy and strategy this game is for you. Awesome themes, interesting haracters and a huge game.
The "bad" part is that to have the complete game you need to put in some extra cash for the dlc:s and previous game.
Still, incredible graphics and very good gameplay

Good storyline , graphics are good but to be fair the ai stinks the battles are dull and the only way the computer wins is by giving it massive buffs .... probably fun to play other players as the mechanics are there. Not suprised to find most of the game under a pay wall but not impressed considering the core of the campaign gameplay isn't that good. Gameplay is everything this seems like it was made in 2010 wont be buying another.
this game is so hard and addicting lets you choose a legendary lord and make it stronger this game i strongly recommend this game might be my fav game right now

I enjoy this game because of the challenge it provides. The graphics and overall presentation are excellent. The game mechanics are, for the most part, very well orchestrated and thought out. With that said, there are things that could be improved on, mainly spell variety. There are many Lores to choose from, but the spells within each lore is just a duplicate spell from a different lore. The name may be different but it is essentially the same spell. Overall, I would give the game two thumbs up and, if you like fantasy, I believe you would like this game too.

The drums in my head pound as I sit in my chair, voices whisper sweet nothings to me as I take a deep breath. What am I? Who am I? I cannot answer these questions as I look up at my screen and realize i've spent over 11 hours on my Mortal empires campagin and i've missed like, 2 full meals. The pounding in my head and the whispering could probably be explained by the dyhydration I am now suffering from due to binge playing this game for 11 hours straight.

40,000/10 this game made me realize that i miss my family and should go talk to them or something.
